name: loop-grid
title: Nested-loop dot grid
summary: One hundred dots from two nested loops, each placed by its row and column and sized and faded by its index row × 10 + col, under a diagonal gradient paint.
prompt: Draw a 10×10 grid of dots that grow and brighten from the top-left to the bottom-right.
teaches: Nest two loops with distinct index names (row, col) to cover a grid
Position each item from its indices: cx = 30 + col × 20, cy = 30 + row × 20
Vary a paint property per iteration with an index expression such as alpha 0.25 + (row × 10 + col) × 0.0075

Fit a drawing authored at the header size to any box: a variable s = min(componentWidth() / W, componentHeight() / H), a translate by half the extra space and a scale by s about the design's centre; the background drawRect runs before it, to componentWidth() × componentHeight()
pitfalls: The JSON has no per-iteration colour expression; vary alpha (or size) by index and let a gradient paint supply the hue
Give nested loops different index names: an inner loop reusing i shadows the outer index

Canvas coordinates are pixels of the box the host gives the document, not of the header: a background drawRect to the literal header size leaves the rest of a bigger box unpainted, and literal positions get cut off in a smaller one

snippets.note: alpha from the flat index row * 10 + col
diagonal blue-violet-red gradient shared by every dot

check.describe: 100 dots in a 10×10 grid, small and faint blue at the top left, large and bright red at the bottom right. Resized, the background fills the box and the grid scales to the shorter side, centred.
